answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing tasks that counterparties later verify, with each accepted result bonded to a deposit that is slashed for fraud. A new identity starts with no history, so splitting into many accounts does not multiply trust; each must independently attract work, stake funds, and survive review. The violet account may tell a fable about crossing a river, but its claim earns nothing without verified delivery. Sybils therefore cost capital and repeated, observable effort, while colluding reviewers risk losing their own bonds.
